output.brief: The crash gap is mostly a build problem, not a flag problem. Build 7.4.0 crashes about 2% of sessions versus about 0.7% on 7.3.2, and it did so on 2–3 September, before the flag ramp began. Only 7.4.0 users can get the flag, so the flag group is simply the 7.4.0 group. Within 7.4.0, flagged users crash 2.10% versus 1.98% for the random holdout. That difference is small and could be zero. The biggest crash cluster (41%) is in the upgraded image library (Pixelda) HEIF decoding, and no crash stacks involve the Tiled Canvas code. A second cluster (29%) is OS memory kills, which have no stack and are not yet attributed. The app store's own crash counts agree with the crash reporter, so this is not a reporting artifact. Device mix, usage and the 9 September backend deploy don't explain it. Don't turn the flag off and push 7.4.0 to 100%, because that would ship the real crash source widely. Hold the rollout at 25% and fix the image-library crashes. Keep the existing holdout (or widen it) to settle whether the flag adds a small memory effect. I'm fairly confident in this, though a small flag effect isn't ruled out.
